extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, and USPTO examiners handling petitions/applications under 37 CFR 1.47 and related practitioner certifications under 37 CFR 1.4 / 10.18
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and evidentiary standards for filing an application or petition under 37 CFR 1.47 (filing on behalf of an inventor who cannot be found or refuses to sign) and related representation/certification obligations under 37 CFR 1.4 and 10.18. Covers proof of unavailability/refusal, proprietary interest, processing, rights of nonsigning inventors, and practitioner certifications/sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of 37 CFR 1.47
rubrics_metrics.description: These provisions allow a “person” with a demonstrated proprietary interest to make application “on behalf of and as agent for” an inventor who “cannot be found or reached after diligent effort” or who refuses to sign the application oath or declaration. Where 37 CFR 1.47(a) is available, application cannot be made under 37 CFR 1.47(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term “person” includes juristic entities (e.g., corporations). 37 CFR 1.47 is limited to situations where the inventor cannot be found/reached after diligent effort or refuses to sign; it is not an alternative to other provisions (e.g., 37 CFR 1.42 or 35 U.S.C. 117) when those provisions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration requirement for 37 CFR 1.47(b) applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: The 37 CFR 1.47(b) applicant must make the oath required by 37 CFR 1.63 and 1.64 or 1.175.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a corporation is the 1.47(b) applicant, an officer (President, Vice‑President, Secretary, Treasurer, or Chief Executive Officer) should normally sign the oath/declaration. A corporation may authorize any person, including a registered attorney or agent, to sign on its behalf, but where an attorney/agent signs on behalf of a corporation, either proof of the attorney's/agent's authority (a statement signed by an appropriate corporate officer) must be submitted, or the attorney/agent may state that he/she is authorized. An inventor may not authorize another individual to act as his/her agent to sign the application oath or declaration on his/her behalf. Where an application is executed by one other than the inventor, the declaration must state the nonsigning inventor’s full name, residence, post office address, and citizenship; the title/position of the person signing should be stated if signing on behalf of a corporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of relationship to inventor (37 CFR 1.64)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 37 CFR 1.47(b) applicant must state his or her relationship to the inventor as required by 37 CFR 1.64.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the specific relationship information as required by the cited regulation (e.g., assignee, employer, officer of corporation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof that inventor cannot be found/reaches or refuses to execute
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be accompanied by proof that the inventor (1) cannot be found or reached after a diligent effort or (2) refuses to execute the application papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a statement of facts fully describing the exact facts relied on to establish diligent effort. Temporary unavailability (vacation, out of town) or hospitalization/unconsciousness is not an acceptable reason for 1.47 (37 CFR 1.43 may be available). The statement should be signed, where possible, by someone with firsthand knowledge; hearsay is not normally acceptable. Documentary evidence (internet searches, certified mail return receipts, cover letters, telegrams, etc.) supporting inability to find/reach should be included and the steps taken to locate the inventor should be recited. The statement should contain facts, not conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof when inventor refuses to join
rubrics_metrics.description: If refusal to sign is the reason for filing under 37 CFR 1.47, the circumstances of presentation of the application papers and the refusal must be specified in a statement of facts by the person who presented the papers and/or to whom the refusal was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send a copy of the application papers to the last known address or the inventor’s counsel. Refusal must be shown: for oral refusals, provide who was present, the time and place; statements by someone not present at the refusal will not be accepted. For written refusals, include a copy (redacted if necessary to remove unrelated material). Proof that a bona fide attempt to present the entire application (specification, claims, drawings, oath/declaration) was made may be sufficient. If the applicant concludes refusal occurred, all supporting facts and documentary evidence should be stated and submitted, and any reason given by the inventor should be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of last known address
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed pursuant to 37 CFR 1.47 must state the last known address of the nonsigning inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The address should be the last known address at which the inventor customarily receives mail—ordinarily the last known residence. Because the inventor will be notified, additional addresses where the inventor may be reached should also be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prima facie proof of proprietary interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The 37 CFR 1.47(b) applicant must make out a prima facie case (1) that the invention has been assigned to him or her or (2) that the inventor has agreed in writing to assign the invention to him or her or (3) otherwise demonstrate a proprietary interest in the subject matter of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assigned, submit a copy of the assignment in English that clearly indicates the invention described was assigned to the applicant; a statement under 37 CFR 3.73(b) by the assignee should also be submitted. An assignment to obtain a filing date solely for a 1.47(b) application is not considered an assignment under 35 U.S.C. 118 and 37 CFR 1.47(b). If relying on an agreement to assign (e.g., employment agreement), submit the agreement; if assignment depends on conditions being met, establish by a statement of facts from someone with firsthand knowledge that conditions were met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrating proprietary interest without assignment/agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention has not been assigned and there is no written agreement to assign, the 37 CFR 1.47(b) applicant must demonstrate that he or she otherwise has sufficient proprietary interest in the subject matter to justify filing the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proprietary interest obtained other than by assignment or agreement to assign may be demonstrated by an appropriate legal memorandum concluding that a court of competent jurisdiction would, by the weight of authority, award title to the applicant. Supporting facts should be made of record by affidavit/declaration of a person with firsthand knowledge. The legal memorandum should be prepared and signed by an attorney familiar with the jurisdiction’s law. Provide English translations of foreign statutes/decisions relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of necessity / irreparable damage
rubrics_metrics.description: The 37 CFR 1.47(b) applicant must prove that the filing of the application is necessary (1) to preserve the rights of the parties or (2) to prevent irreparable damage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irreparable damage may be established by a showing (statement) that a filing date is necessary to preserve rights or prevent irreparable harm. Include factual support for the necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.47 and deceased inventors/legal representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.47 should not be considered an alternative to 37 CFR 1.42 or 35 U.S.C. 117 since the language 'cannot be found or reached after diligent effort' has no reasonable application to a deceased inventor. However, 37 CFR 1.47 does apply where a known legal representative of a deceased inventor cannot be found or reached after diligent effort, or refuses to make application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases involving deceased inventors, use the provisions applicable to deceased inventors unless the legal representative is unavailable/refuses; when filing under 1.47 for a legal representative, provide last known address of the representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and acceptance of a 37 CFR 1.47 application
rubrics_metrics.description: A filing date is assigned to an application deposited pursuant to 37 CFR 1.47 provided the requirements of 37 CFR 1.53(b) are met. When papers deposited pursuant to 37 CFR 1.47 are found acceptable, the Office of Petitions enters a decision to that effect in the file and a notice will be published identifying the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A filing receipt will be sent to the applicant; the application or an electronic message concerning the petition will be forwarded to the Office of Petitions for consideration. The USPTO will notify the nonsigning inventor or legal representative at the last known address. Notices are not repeated in continuations or divisional applications if a copy of the declaration and decision are filed as permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of the nonsigning inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: The nonsigning inventor may protest his/her designation, is entitled to inspect any paper in the application, order copies at the price set by 37 CFR 1.19, and make his/her position of record. The nonsigning inventor may join in the application by filing an appropriate 37 CFR 1.63 oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The nonsigning inventor may arrange to do the foregoing through a registered patent attorney/agent. Inter partes proceedings will not be instituted in 37 CFR 1.47 cases; the nonsigning inventor is not entitled to a hearing and is not entitled to prosecute the application if status under 37 CFR 1.47 has been accorded or proprietary interest has been shown to the Office’s satisfaction. If the nonsigning inventor joins, he/she cannot revoke or give a power of attorney without agreement of the 1.47 applicant. The patent must issue to the inventor; a nonsigning inventor who claims sole inventorship may file his/her own application and seek an interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner action after a 37 CFR 1.47 petition is filed
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner receives an application in which a petition under 37 CFR 1.47 has been filed, he or she must check the file to determine that the petition has been decided by the Office of Petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petition has not been decided by the Office of Petitions, the application, or an electronic message concerning the petition, must be forwarded to the Office of Petitions for appropriate action. After acceptance, the examiner proceeds with examination in the usual manner; papers filed by an inventor who did not originally join will be placed in the file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of papers constitutes certification (37 CFR 1.4(d)(4) / 10.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: The presentation to the Office (whether by signing, filing, submitting, or later advocating) of any paper by a party constitutes a certification under 37 CFR 10.18(b). Violations may result in imposition of sanctions under 10.18(c); practitioners may also be subject to disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By presenting a paper, the party certifies the statements are true and that a reasonable inquiry has been made. This has eliminated many separate verification requirements for statements by persons not registered to practice; verification requirements for oaths/declarations remain in specific sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications as to signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: A person submitting a document signed by another is obligated to have a reasonable basis to believe that the signature was actually inserted by that person and should retain evidence of authenticity. A person inserting a signature certifies that the inserted signature is his or her own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of the signature certifications may result in sanctions under 10.18(c) and (d). Retain evidence of authenticity (e.g., proof of authority) when filing documents signed by others. Practitioners should be mindful of these obligations when submitting/filing signed documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive certifications required by 37 CFR 10.18(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: By presenting any paper to the USPTO the party certifies: (1) all statements of the party’s own knowledge are true and statements on information and belief are believed to be true; and (2) to the best of the party’s knowledge, information and belief formed after a reasonable inquiry that (i) the paper is not presented for an improper purpose, (ii) the claims/legal contentions are warranted by existing law or by a nonfrivolous argument, (iii) allegations/factual contentions have evidentiary support or likely will after reasonable opportunity, and (iv) denials of factual contentions are warranted or reasonably based on a lack of information or belief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These certifications mirror Rule 11(b) standards. Parties must conduct an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances before filing. Tolerance exists for allegations made on information and belief but the party has a continuing duty not to persist in unsupported contentions after reasonable opportunity for investigation/discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and sanctions for violating 10.18(b)(2)(i)-(iv)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of 10.18(b)(2)(i)–(iv) are, after notice and reasonable opportunity to respond, subject to such sanctions as deemed appropriate by the Commissioner, which may include holding facts established, returning papers, precluding a party from filing a paper or contesting an issue, imposing a monetary sanction, requiring a terminal disclaimer for the period of the delay, or terminating the proceedings in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any practitioner violating these provisions may also be subject to disciplinary action (see 10.23(c)(15)). Sanctions are discretionary and can be combined. False or misleading statements by applicants or practitioners during prosecution have resulted in patents being held unenforceable in case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable inquiry standard and practitioner reliance on client/third-party information
rubrics_metrics.description: The certification requires that the party's belief be formed after an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances, an objective/negligence-type standard similar to Fed. R. Civ. P. 11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amount of investigation required depends on the time available and the probability that more investigation will turn up important evidence; the rule does not require steps that are not cost-justified. A practitioner's 'reasonable inquiry' duty is met when relying upon information from the applicant or third party so long as the practitioner has no knowledge contradictory to that information or reason to suspect it was provided to violate 10.18 (e.g., to cause delay). It is advisable for practitioners to advise clients that information provided must be reliable and not misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of verification and interaction with verification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 10.18(b)(1) has allowed the USPTO to eliminate separate verification requirements previously contained in many sections for statements of facts by persons not registered to practice; however, the verification requirement for statements submitted under oath or declaration (37 CFR 1.68) is retained in a number of sections (e.g., 1.63, 1.130, 1.131, 1.132, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand which statements still require separate oath/declaration verification and which are covered by the general certification under 10.18(b)(1). When submitting statements under oath/declaration, comply with the specific verification rules in the cited sections.
